quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'morning' and 'coffee'.
quests.explanation: Say the first syllable louder, higher in pitch, and a bit longer than the syllables that follow.
quests.textToSpeak: My morning coffee is the best part of my schedule.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'morning', 'coffee', and 'schedule'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'teacher' and 'difficult'.
quests.explanation: Push extra energy into the first syllable — make it louder and clearer than the rest of the word.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher gave us a difficult homework project.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'teacher', 'difficult', 'homework', and 'project'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'manager' and 'meeting'.
quests.explanation: Give the first syllable more punch: raise your pitch slightly and let it ring out longer.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager scheduled a meeting about the budget.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'manager', 'meeting', and 'budget'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'journey' and 'visit'.
quests.explanation: Land hard on the first syllable, then let the rest of the word trail off more quietly.
quests.textToSpeak: Our journey included a visit to the airport.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'journey', 'visit', and 'airport'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'grandmother' and 'wonderful'.
quests.explanation: Emphasize the very first beat of the word — louder, clearer, and held a touch longer.
quests.textToSpeak: My grandmother told a wonderful story about her childhood.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'grandmother', 'wonderful', 'story', and 'childhood'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'customer' and 'discount'.
quests.explanation: Put the weight of the word on its first syllable, keeping the following syllables lighter.
quests.textToSpeak: The customer asked about the discount on this product.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'customer', 'discount', and 'product'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'breakfast' and 'customers'.
quests.explanation: Start strong: stress the first syllable with more volume and pitch, then ease off after it.
quests.textToSpeak: The chef prepared a delicious breakfast for the customers.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'breakfast' and 'customers'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'company' and 'gadget'.
quests.explanation: The first syllable should stand out — say it with more force than the syllables after it.
quests.textToSpeak: The company released a new gadget with better software.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'company', 'gadget', 'better', and 'software'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'doctor' and 'healthy'.
quests.explanation: Lead with energy on the first syllable, then let your voice relax through the rest of the word.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor recommended a healthy diet and regular exercise.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'doctor', 'healthy', 'diet', 'regular', and 'exercise'.

quests.hint: Stress the first syllable in 'orchestra' and 'wonderful'.
quests.explanation: Make the opening syllable the loudest, clearest part of the word, then soften the rest.
quests.textToSpeak: The orchestra performed a wonderful concert at the theater.
quests.phoneticHint: Land the stress up front in 'orchestra', 'wonderful', 'concert', and 'theater'.

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'record' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'record' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: As a noun, stress falls on the first syllable; as a verb, the same word shifts stress to the second.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll record the song, then play the record for everyone.
quests.phoneticHint: First 'record' is the verb (re-CORD); second 'record' is the noun (RE-cord).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'permit' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'permit' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: Notice how the word changes meaning with its stress: first-syllable stress for the noun, second for the verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher will permit a permit slip for the trip.
quests.phoneticHint: 'Will permit' is the verb (per-MIT); 'a permit slip' is the noun (PER-mit).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'contract' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'contract' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: The noun version stresses the front of the word; the verb version pushes the stress to the back.
quests.textToSpeak: We need to contract a contract with the new vendor.
quests.phoneticHint: 'To contract' is the verb (con-TRACT); 'a contract' is the noun (CON-tract).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'increase' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'increase' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: Shift your stress from the first syllable (noun) to the second syllable (verb) as the word's role changes.
quests.textToSpeak: The airline plans to increase the increase in baggage fees.
quests.phoneticHint: 'To increase' is the verb (in-CREASE); 'the increase' is the noun (IN-crease).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'object' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'object' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: Same spelling, different job: stress the start for the noun, stress the middle for the verb.
quests.textToSpeak: She will object if I bring up that old object.
quests.phoneticHint: 'Will object' is the verb (ob-JECT); 'that old object' is the noun (OB-ject).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'produce' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'produce' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: Listen for the stress moving — forward for the noun, backward for the verb form of this word.
quests.textToSpeak: The store will produce more produce for the weekend sale.
quests.phoneticHint: 'Will produce' is the verb (pro-DUCE); 'more produce' is the noun (PRO-duce).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'import' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'import' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: The word's meaning depends entirely on where you place the stress: front for noun, back for verb.
quests.textToSpeak: We import spices, since the import tastes better fresh.
quests.phoneticHint: 'We import' is the verb (im-PORT); 'the import' is the noun (IM-port).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'export' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'export' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: As you switch from noun to verb, let the stress slide from the first syllable to the second.
quests.textToSpeak: We export the software, and the export takes minutes.
quests.phoneticHint: 'We export' is the verb (ex-PORT); 'the export' is the noun (EX-port).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: verb 'conduct' (2nd syllable) vs. noun 'conduct' (1st syllable).
quests.explanation: This word carries its meaning in its stress pattern: first syllable for the thing, second for the action.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager will conduct an interview about his team's conduct.
quests.phoneticHint: 'Will conduct' is the verb (con-DUCT); 'team's conduct' is the noun (CON-duct).

quests.hint: Hear the stress move: noun 'protest' (1st syllable) vs. verb 'protest' (2nd syllable).
quests.explanation: Stress up front turns it into a noun; stress further back turns the very same word into a verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The protest grew loud as fans began to protest the result.
quests.phoneticHint: 'The protest' is the noun (PRO-test); 'to protest' is the verb (pro-TEST).

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'banana' and 'sofa'.
quests.explanation: Let unstressed syllables go soft and lazy — that quick, relaxed 'uh' sound is the schwa.
quests.textToSpeak: I take a banana and a sofa cushion to relax.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in the article 'a' (twice), and inside 'banana' and 'sofa'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'lesson' and 'about'.
quests.explanation: Don't fully pronounce unstressed vowels; let them collapse into a quick, neutral 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher gave a lesson about the famous author.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'a', 'lesson', 'about', 'the', and 'author'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'about' and 'agenda'.
quests.explanation: Relax your mouth completely for unstressed syllables — they blur into a short, flat 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager wrote a memo about the agenda.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'The', 'a', 'about', and twice inside 'agenda'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'famous' and 'area'.
quests.explanation: The schwa is English's laziest vowel: barely open your mouth and let it come out as 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: We visited a famous area near the harbor.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'a', 'famous', 'area', 'the', and 'harbor'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'cousin' and 'sister'.
quests.explanation: Unstressed vowels lose their full sound and shrink down to a quick, colorless 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: My cousin and my sister adore their grandma.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'cousin', 'sister', and 'adore'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'sofa' and 'camera'.
quests.explanation: Keep your mouth relaxed and central for unstressed syllables — they all sound like a soft 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: I bought a sofa and a camera at the market.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'a' (twice), 'sofa', 'camera', and 'the'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'banana' and 'pasta'.
quests.explanation: Don't work hard on unstressed vowels; let them reduce naturally into a light 'uh' sound.
quests.textToSpeak: The banana bread and the pasta were delicious.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'The', 'banana', 'the', and 'pasta'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'camera' and 'modem'.
quests.explanation: The schwa takes almost no effort — just a relaxed, neutral 'uh' in the unstressed syllables.
quests.textToSpeak: The camera and the modem need a quick update.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'The', 'camera', 'the', 'modem', and 'a'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'doctor' and 'advice'.
quests.explanation: Unstressed syllables flatten into this short, effortless 'uh' — English's most common vowel sound.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor gave advice about the proper diet.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'The', 'doctor', 'advice', 'about', and 'proper'.

quests.hint: Focus on the relaxed schwa [ə] in 'cinema' and 'drama'.
quests.explanation: Let go of precision in unstressed syllables; they naturally reduce to a quick, relaxed 'uh'.
quests.textToSpeak: The cinema showed a drama about a famous singer.
quests.phoneticHint: Hear [ə] in 'The', 'cinema', 'a', 'drama', 'about', and 'famous'.
